best_moment.what: Putting my own name on the submission to the salary committee. It felt like the game's actual point and I was the one who chose to go there.

worst_moment.what: The run of single-option years (PQ, walkabouts, Meet-the-People) where I tapped one button and watched STAND drop with no say. It felt like homework.

skip_year.why: Part of the Y27-31 stretch of single-option years. Nothing to decide, STAND just fell, and I can't remember a thing from it.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y8 background check: answered only what was asked, folder may surface
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Never clearly came back. The ending's EXPOSURE line says my file is clean and boring.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y7 took the tea invitation into politics
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The ending says the party had its own estimate for me (Senior Minister of State) and nobody told me. That explains the rumours.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y46 rumour: left off the Leadership Programme list, no reason given
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The ending translates 'steady' as my work earning a promotion that my ceiling refused, told 3 times.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y38 note to the newer MP who quoted me
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Legacy line: people I trained quote me and two say I'm why they stayed.

answer.held_back_by: A hidden ceiling in the file and the party's low estimate of me, which I never saw while playing. Probably also my pushing on pay indicators and the low STAND from all the forced years.
answer.ending_fair_why: Deputy PM at 72 with INTEG 100 is a good result, and the declassified card explained the rumours I'd been confused by. But it felt a bit unfair that the ceiling was hidden and I only found out at the end.
answer.chase_next: The one where I ask for the hard ministry earlier than 57 and break the ceiling sooner, to see if I can get to PM or what the top actually looks like.
answer.play_again_why: The good bits were great but the long stretches of single-option years wore me out. I'd need a break, and maybe a shorter run.

tone_breaks.line: You served. The service continued. Both of these facts are entirely unremarkable and that is the highest compliment the system can pay.
tone_breaks.note: A bit smug and knowing, though I did kind of like it.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is really about being confirmed and ceilings in your file, the rumours and the 'steady' translation. The pay was just the backdrop for me.

finalScreen:
DARREN LIM · THE FINAL POSITION
Retired, Honourably

You served. The service continued. Both of these facts are entirely unremarkable and that is the highest compliment the system can pay.

RETIRED AS Deputy Prime Minister
AT AGE 72
LIFETIME EARNINGS $61.07M
INTEGRITY 100

DECLASSIFIED
YOUR CEILING: When you joined, your file put no ceiling on you inside the service. Most people's files do.
THE PARTY'S ESTIMATE: When you won your seat, the party made its own: Senior Minister of State. Nobody told you that either.
THE YEAR IT CHANGED: At 57, in The Reshuffle, you chose "Ask for the hard ministry nobody wants." It raised your ceiling to Deputy Prime Minister.
THE RUMOURS, TRANSLATED: "Your reporting officer describes your trajectory as "steady"." meant: your work had earned a promotion and your ceiling refused it. You were told this 3 times.
EXPOSURE: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
LEGACY: People you trained quote you in rooms you will never enter. Two of them say you are the reason they stayed.
